clean_story:
Vibrations in air. Emotions in the brain.

The word "sound" comes from the Latin sonus, meaning what is heard, because sound is simply our perception of vibrating air molecules hitting the eardrum.

A baby’s cry triggers a rush of oxytocin in listeners, bonding parent and child before words exist. A horror movie’s low rumble at 20 Hertz makes your skin prickle—your body reacts before you realize why. Fast tempos above 120 beats per minute can quicken pulses, while slow, steady rhythms like a heartbeat calm the nervous system. Music therapists use this to ease pain: patients listening to tailored playlists report needing less medication. Even silence shapes emotion—studies show two minutes of quiet lower blood pressure more than relaxing music.

Three related subjects are music therapy, acoustic resonance, and fear response.
